name: When do I need to replace my shower valve instead of just the trim?

mainEntity.name: When do I need to replace my shower valve instead of just the trim?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need a new shower valve when you experience inconsistent water temperatures, sudden drops in pressure, chronic drips, or when switching to a different trim manufacturer. Old valves without pressure-balancing or thermostatic protection can cause sudden scalding when someone runs water elsewhere in the house. If you are updating shower trim aesthetics, most modern brands require a proprietary valve body inside the wall. If your current valve is several decades old, replacing it during a remodel prevents having to cut into walls later to fix an internal leak.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace the valve if you have pressure drops, temperature fluctuations, leaks, or if your new trim is incompatible with the existing rough-in valve brand.
